QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_70

question.text: Under SAS-1300 the 'women-owned-account' indicator should be disaggregated by:

answer.text: Age, rural/urban, SC/ST/OBC/General, income quintile, and first-time-or-not — to reveal inclusion patterns

explanation.text: The Logic: A meaningful financial-inclusion indicator like "women-owned-account" is conceptually more informative when disaggregated by age, rural/urban location, social category (SC/ST/OBC/General), income quintile and first-time-or-not status. This multi-dimensional view reveals whether the programme actually reached marginalised sub-segments rather than just adding accounts in aggregate. The Trap: A single total count masks distribution and inclusion patterns entirely. Phone numbers are personal identifiers, not disaggregation categories. Hairstyle is irrelevant to financial inclusion. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026), in its SAS-1300 financial-inclusion case material, supports composition fields such as Age, Gender, Occupation, Education, Family Income, Sources of Income and prior/formal tool usage, but the specific framing of "women-owned-account" disaggregation by caste/community, income quintile, rural/urban and first-time status is not found on the pages reviewed. The reasoning above reflects general financial-inclusion measurement practice.
